creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Fourier Series

Harmonics

description: Build square, triangle, sawtooth, pulse-train and hand-drawn periodic waveforms from their first N harmonics. A time plot overlays the partial sum on the waveform, and bar charts show the amplitude and phase of each harmonic or the cosine and sine coefficients.

educational.topic: Fourier series, Fourier coefficients and convergence of partial sums
learningObjectives: Explain a Fourier series as a sum of harmonics of the fundamental frequency
Compare the harmonic content of square, triangle, sawtooth and pulse waveforms
Describe how the partial sum converges as harmonics are added, and what the Gibbs phenomenon is
Relate the coefficients a_n and b_n to the amplitude and phase of each harmonic

controls.label: Play / Pause
controls.description: Adds one harmonic every 0.55 s; starts paused

controls.label: Hover a bar to select a harmonic, click a bar to switch it off, drag in the time plot to draw the custom waveform

equations: x(t) = a0 + sum over n of [a_n cos(n w0 t) + b_n sin(n w0 t)], w0 = 2 pi / T
c_n = (a_n - j b_n) / 2, amplitude = sqrt(a_n^2 + b_n^2) = 2 |c_n|
square wave: b_n = 4 / (pi n) for odd n
triangle wave: b_n = 8 (-1)^((n-1)/2) / (pi^2 n^2) for odd n
pulse train with duty cycle d: a0 = d, a_n = 2 sin(pi n d) / (pi n)
assumptions: Coefficients of the four standard waveforms are closed-form; the custom waveform is integrated numerically over 512 samples
The partial sum, rms error and overshoot are evaluated on 4096 points per period
The overshoot is the amount by which the highest peak or lowest trough of the partial sum lies beyond the waveform, divided by the jump height

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through synthesis: add one harmonic at a time and compare the partial sum with the waveform
keyQuestions: Which harmonics does each waveform contain, and how fast do their amplitudes fall?
Does the overshoot near a jump disappear as more harmonics are added?
What symmetry makes a waveform need only sine terms or only cosine terms?
commonMisconceptions: Adding enough harmonics removes the overshoot at a discontinuity
Every periodic waveform contains all harmonics
Phase does not affect the shape of a waveform
assessmentOpportunities: Check b_1, b_3 and b_5 of the square wave against 4/(pi n)
Record the overshoot for N = 1, 3, 5, 9, 21 and 50 and explain the trend
